doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Rod Stewart's Downtown Train sped up to B flat
summary: The key was raised from G to B flat, making his string and English horn writing sound odd but work; Trevor Horn's fix.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Very true. Very true. And again, if I’m arranging a pop record for example, I’m always thinking of what the key is, what the vocalist is, and what can surround it in a certain way. So for example an interesting one in terms of the pop music was Rod Stewart’s version of “Downtown Train,” the Tom Waits song, because we recorded it in the key of G and then he found that his voice — because he’d abstained from smoking and worked out and whatever, it was too low. So they vari-sped it up to B flat. And this was the days before autotune and computerized — I don’t know how they did it but what happened was the entire arrangement sounded weird. It worked but it was weird. All the vibratos of the strings and woodwind were wrong. They were ethereal — other worldly. And I’d written for two English horns that were at the top of their range. Once it was pushed up to B flat they were above where they would normally be so if I’d have known I was going to be in B flat I would have written for oboes. If I’d known I was going to be in B flat I wouldn’t have written the strings so high but it all worked. So it was serendipity.
Wow. I have never heard of such a thing. And so it didn’t speed up the music.

No I don’t know how they did it. I mean Trevor Horn who produced it, in his new book, has explained how he did it, which there was some sort of film — something that was used by movie editors that he appropriated and he replaced the arrangement with synthesized — until the point where they could get it to actually sound like it should have done, and then they put back the original chart. I mean it wasn’t as simple as tweaking a knob and pushing the whole thing up a tone, or well a tone would have been a lot. But this is a tone and a half. It’s insanity.
